'''''Protea grandiceps''''', commonly known as '''rooisuikerbos''', '''suikerbos''' or '''red sugarbush''',<ref name=atlas/> is a flowering shrub that belongs to the ''[[Protea]]'' genus and is native to south western parts of [[South Africa]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.treetags.co.za/national-list-of-indigenous-trees/|title=National List of Indigenous Trees|publisher=Treetags|access-date=10 July 2020}}</ref> The shrub was listed as a near [[threatened species]] in 2006 according to the [[South African National Biodiversity Institute]].<ref name=redlist/>

==Description==
The shrub is round and grows {{cvt|2|m}} high and blooms from September to January.<ref name=atlas>{{cite web|url=https://www.proteaatlas.org.za/sugar2.htm|title=Bearded Sugarbushes - ''Proteas''|access-date=10 July 2020|publisher=The Protea Atlas Project}}</ref>
Fire destroys the plant but the seeds survive. The seed is stored in a cap and spread by the wind. The plant is unisexual. Pollination occurs through the action of birds. The tree's national number is 89.2.<ref name=plantz/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://biodiversityexplorer.info/plants/proteaceae/protea_grandiceps.htm|title=''Protea grandiceps'' (Red sugarbush)|access-date=10 July 2020|work=biodiversity explorer|publisher=Iziko Museums of South Africa}}</ref><ref name=redlist>{{cite web|url=http://redlist.sanbi.org/species.php?species=799-49|title=Red Sugarbush|access-date=10 July 2020|work=Red List of South African Plants|publisher=[[South African National Biodiversity Institute]]|year=2012}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first formally described by the botanist [[Leopold Trattinnick]], the [[botanical name|specific epithet]] means ''large head'' and is derived from the [[Latin]] words ''grandis'' meaning ''great'' or ''large'' and ''ceps'' meaning ''head'' in reference to the flower-heads.<ref name=plantz/>

==Distribution==
The plant is [[endemism|endemic]] to [[South Africa]] and is found in the [[Cape Peninsula]], [[Hottentots Holland Mountains]], Riviersonderend Mountains, Langeberg, Outeniqua Mountains, Tsitsikamma Mountains, Winterhoek Mountains and Kamanassie Mountains<ref name=plantz>{{cite web|url=http://pza.sanbi.org/protea-grandiceps|title=''Protea grandiceps'' Tratt.|access-date=10 July 2020|work=PlantZAfrica|publisher=South African National Biodiversity Institute}}</ref> where it is commonly situated on stony crevices on dry upper mountain slopes at elevations of {{cvt|1200|to|1700|m}}. It is spread over a total area of around {{cvt|652|km2}} composed of fragmented populations.<ref name=redlist/>
